patients.summary: Elementary school teacher from Westhampton who joined in 2020 with acute promyelocytic leukemia (2018) in remission. SLE diagnosed 2023 on hydroxychloroquine; diminished ovarian reserve 2024; APL relapse 10/2025 treated with ATRA to a second remission; corticosteroid-induced psychosis 4/2026 during a lupus flare, resolved.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

CC: establish care.

HPI: 32 y/o woman, elementary school teacher, new to the practice. Her one medical issue is acute promyelocytic leukemia, diagnosed 2018 when she was 30 and treated at an outside cancer center. She says treatment is finished and she was told she is in complete remission. Does not have the details of her treatment with her; release signed, records requested from the cancer center and from her prior PCP.
Currently feels well. Good energy. Denies fevers, sweats, weight change, bruising, nosebleeds, gum bleeding, joint pain, rash.

PMH: APL 2018, treated, in CR.
PSH: none.
Meds: vitamin D3 2000 units daily (OTC).
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother - rheumatoid arthritis. Maternal aunt - SLE. Father - HTN. She also mentions hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia "runs in the family," but isn't sure which relative has it.
SH: teaches elementary school. Never smoker. No alcohol. No drug use.
GYN: menses regular.
Health maintenance: cervical screening done at prior office 2019, told normal. Not sure when last tetanus shot was.

ROS: negative except as above.

Exam: BP 116/69, HR 72, T 36.7, SpO2 96%, wt 62.0 kg, ht 163.1 cm, BMI 23.3.
Well-appearing, NAD. Skin: no petechiae, no bruising, no rash. HEENT: conjunctivae pink, oropharynx clear, gums normal. Neck: supple, no lymphadenopathy, thyroid normal. CV: RRR, normal S1/S2, no murmurs. Lungs: CTA bilaterally. Abd: soft, nontender, no hepatosplenomegaly. Ext: no edema. Neuro: alert, CN intact, strength and gait normal.

PHQ-2: 0.

A/P:
1. Acute promyelocytic leukemia, in complete remission (dx 2018, outside treatment completed). Asymptomatic, exam benign. CBC w/ diff and CMP today as baseline. Will review cancer center records when they arrive.
2. Health maintenance: flu vaccine given today. Cervical screening 2019 normal per pt - confirm on records; next due 2024. HIV/HCV screening at her physical. Tetanus status - check prior records.
3. Vitamin D3 OTC - continue.

RTC ~1 year for annual physical, sooner prn.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Nilda,
Nice meeting you yesterday. Your labs look good. Blood counts are healthy (hemoglobin 13.5, white count 7.4, platelets 262); the monocyte percentage in the differential is a hair over the lab's cutoff at 9%, which doesn't mean anything on its own. Kidney and liver tests are normal.
We'll be in touch once your records come in. See you next year for your physical.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
OFFICE VISIT

CC: fatigue, joint pain, facial rash.

HPI: 35F with APL in remission (2018) presents with roughly 5 months of tiredness that sleep doesn't fix and aching joints - wrists and knees mostly. Separately notices a red rash across her cheeks after time outdoors in the sun, lasting a day or two. No fevers. No bleeding or bruising. Maternal aunt has SLE.

Meds: folic acid 1 mg, vitamin D3 2000 units.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BP 121/67, HR 63, T 36.4, wt 62.0 kg.
Skin: no rash on the face today. Wrists and knees: no swelling or effusion, full range of motion. Heart RRR, lungs clear, abdomen soft and nontender. No lymphadenopathy.

A/P:
Fatigue + inflammatory-sounding arthralgia + photosensitive facial rash by history, FH of SLE -> concerned for lupus.
- Rheumatology referral placed; asked front desk to push for an early slot. Rheumatology does its own serologies and baseline labs at the consult, so not drawing today.
- Sun protection: broad-spectrum sunscreen, hat for recess duty.
- Call if fever, chest pain, worsening joints.

documents.title: Rheumatology Consultation
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
RHEUMATOLOGY CONSULTATION
Date of service: 04/11/2023
Patient: Nilda Mendez, 35-year-old woman
Referred by: primary care, for fatigue, joint pain and facial rash

Thank you for sending Ms. Mendez to us.

History: She describes about six months of tiredness along with aching in her joints, worst in the wrists and knees, and a rash over her face that comes and goes after she has been out in the sun. She has a history of acute promyelocytic leukemia diagnosed in 2018, treated and in remission.

Medications: folic acid 1 mg daily; vitamin D3 2000 units daily.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family history: mother with rheumatoid arthritis; maternal aunt with systemic lupus erythematosus; father with hypertension.
Social: elementary school teacher. Never smoker, no alcohol.

Examination: BP 109/78, pulse 70, weight 61.5 kg. Malar rash over both cheeks and the nasal bridge. Mild synovitis of both wrists and both knees. No oral ulcers. Heart and lungs normal. No edema.

Laboratory (drawn here 04/11/2023):
- Hemoglobin 10.5 g/dL (low)
- White blood cells 3,500/uL (low)
- Platelets 100,000/uL (low)
- ANA positive, titer 1:640
- Anti-dsDNA positive
- C3 low, C4 low
- Creatinine 0.78 mg/dL
- Urinalysis negative for protein and blood

Impression: Systemic lupus erythematosus, with malar rash and photosensitivity, inflammatory arthritis of the wrists and knees, and leukopenia, anemia and thrombocytopenia that I attribute to lupus. Strongly positive ANA, positive dsDNA and low complements support the diagnosis. Kidney function and urine are normal.

Plan:
1. Hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily, started today.
2. Strict sun protection - broad-spectrum sunscreen, hat, avoid midday sun.
3. Baseline retinal examination for hydroxychloroquine - referral to ophthalmology placed.
4. Return in about 3 months with CBC, C3/C4, creatinine and urinalysis.

Medications at the end of this visit: hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily (new today); folic acid 1 mg daily; vitamin D3 2000 units daily.

Rheumatology

documents.title: New lupus medicine
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, rheumatology told me I have lupus and started me on hydroxychloroquine. I'm still trying to get pregnant. Is this medicine safe if I do get pregnant? I forgot to ask there. Kind of overwhelmed.

documents.title: RE: New lupus medicine
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Nilda, I got the rheumatology letter - I'm sorry, that's a lot to take in at once. Hydroxychloroquine is one of the lupus medicines that is generally continued in pregnancy, so it's not a reason to stop trying. Do keep taking it every day, and please also ask rheumatology at your next visit so they can plan with you. Happy to talk by phone or in person if helpful.

documents.title: Ophthalmology - baseline exam
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
OPHTHALMOLOGY
Date of exam: 05/22/2023
Reason: baseline examination before long-term hydroxychloroquine (SLE).

Visual acuity: 20/20 OD, 20/20 OS. Pupils equal and reactive, no APD. IOP normal OU. Anterior segment unremarkable OU.
Dilated fundus exam: optic nerves healthy; maculae normal with no pigmentary change; periphery flat.
SD-OCT macula: normal foveal contour and outer retinal layers OU.
Automated visual fields 10-2: full OU.

Impression: normal baseline examination; no evidence of retinopathy.
Plan: annual hydroxychloroquine screening beginning after 5 years of use, sooner if visual symptoms.

Ophthalmology baseline exam normal.

Assessment: SLE responding well to hydroxychloroquine. Cytopenias, including the thrombocytopenia, have resolved.
Plan: continue hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily. Labs and visit in about 3 months.

documents.title: Gynecology Consultation
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OBSTETRICS & GYNECOLOGY CONSULTATION
Date of service: 01/10/2024
Reason for referral: no pregnancy after about 18 months of trying.

Many thanks for referring Ms. Mendez. She is a 35-year-old woman who has been trying for a year and a half without conceiving, even though her periods come like clockwork every 28 days. Her history includes systemic lupus erythematosus, quiet on hydroxychloroquine, and acute promyelocytic leukemia treated in 2018 and in remission. Medications: hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily, folic acid 1 mg daily, vitamin D3 2000 units daily. No known drug allergies.
Family history: her mother went through menopause at 38.

Examination: BP 103/78, weight 62.5 kg. General, breast, abdominal and pelvic examinations are unremarkable.

Laboratory (cycle day 3, drawn 01/10/2024):
- TSH 1.7 - normal
- Prolactin 11.9 - normal
- Estradiol - low-normal
- Anti-Mullerian hormone - low
- FSH 14.8 mIU/mL - elevated for early follicular phase

Assessment: diminished ovarian reserve, with an elevated early-follicular FSH, low AMH and low-normal estradiol - hypergonadotropic hypogonadism - in a woman with regular ovulatory-pattern cycles.

Plan: I went through these results with her and what they mean, and we discussed her options in general terms. She would like time to think things over. No treatment started today and no further referral at this time.

Gynecology

documents.title: Same-day Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
SAME-DAY VISIT

CC: fatigue, headaches, bruising.

HPI: 37F with APL 2018 in CR, SLE on HCQ (quiet). About a month of tiredness that doesn't lift and intermittent headaches. Now and then bruises more easily than usual and gums bleed a little with brushing. She puts it down to a stressful stretch at school and poor sleep. No fevers. No nosebleeds, no blood in urine or stool. Headaches mild, no visual change, no focal symptoms.

Meds: hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily, folic acid 1 mg daily, vitamin D3 2000 units daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BP 108/64, HR 64, T 36.5, SpO2 98% - vitals normal.
Mildly pale; conjunctival pallor. Scattered petechiae over both lower legs. Gums without active bleeding. No lymphadenopathy. CV RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft, NT, no hepatosplenomegaly. Neuro nonfocal.

A/P:
Fatigue, headaches, easy bruising, gum bleeding, pallor and petechiae in a woman with prior APL -> worried about relapse.
- Stat CBC w/ diff drawn in office, lab asked to call me directly with results.

documents.title: Hematology/Oncology Admission H&P

documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - HEMATOLOGY/ONCOLOGY ADMISSION HISTORY AND PHYSICAL
Admitted: 10/11/2025 00:50 (received via health information exchange)

Patient: Nilda Mendez, 37-year-old woman.
Reason for admission: pancytopenia; concern for relapse of acute promyelocytic leukemia. Referred by her primary care physician after an outpatient CBC.

HPI: Ms. Mendez had acute promyelocytic leukemia in 2018, treated and in remission since. Over the past month she has had persistent fatigue and headaches that come and go. She has noticed occasional easy bruising and mild bleeding from her gums, which she had attributed to stress and poor sleep. Her primary care physician found mild pallor and petechiae today and a CBC showing hemoglobin 8.4 g/dL, platelets 34,000/mm3 and WBC 2,600/mm3.

PMH: acute promyelocytic leukemia (2018), in remission until now; systemic lupus erythematosus (2023), quiet on hydroxychloroquine; hypergonadotropic hypogonadism / diminished ovarian reserve (2024).
PSH: none.
Home medications: hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily; folic acid 1 mg daily; vitamin D3 2000 units daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: mother - rheumatoid arthritis; maternal aunt - SLE; father - hypertension. Reports a family history of hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia; she does not know which relative.
Social: elementary school teacher; never smoker; no alcohol; no illicit drugs.

Vitals on arrival: normal.
Exam: mild pallor. Scattered petechiae over the lower extremities. No lymphadenopathy. Heart regular without murmur; lungs clear to auscultation. Abdomen soft, nontender, no hepatosplenomegaly. Neurologic exam nonfocal.

Labs: outpatient CBC as above. Admission CMP within normal limits. Urine pregnancy test negative.

Assessment: 37-year-old woman with prior APL now with pancytopenia - relapse of APL is the leading concern.
Plan:
- Bone marrow aspirate and biopsy with cytogenetics/FISH; peripheral smear review.
- Begin tretinoin (ATRA) 45 mg/m2/day in two divided doses now, given the clinical suspicion; pregnancy test negative. Counselled that she must avoid pregnancy while taking ATRA and for one month after stopping.
- Daily CBC, supportive care, bleeding precautions.
- Continue hydroxychloroquine, folic acid, vitamin D3.

documents.title: Hematology/Oncology Discharge Summary
documents.author: hematology/oncology
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admission: 10/11/2025   Discharge: 11/07/2025
Service: Hematology/Oncology

Principal diagnosis: relapsed acute promyelocytic leukemia, t(15;17), PML-RARA positive.
Other diagnoses: systemic lupus erythematosus; hypergonadotropic hypogonadism.

Hospital course:
Admitted from her PCP with pancytopenia (Hgb 8.4, plt 34,000, WBC 2,600) seven years after her first APL. Peripheral smear was reviewed and was consistent with the marrow diagnosis. Bone marrow biopsy 10/13 showed involvement by acute promyelocytic leukemia with t(15;17) - relapse.
Tretinoin (ATRA) 45 mg/m2/day in two divided doses (40 mg twice daily) was started on admission after a negative pregnancy test and continued throughout. She was counselled on avoiding pregnancy while on ATRA and for a month afterward. She tolerated treatment and her counts steadily recovered.
Day-before-discharge CBC (11/06): WBC 3.5, Hgb 9.7, platelets 134 - recovering.

Condition at discharge: stable, ambulatory, eating well.

Discharge medications:
- Tretinoin 10 mg capsules: 40 mg by mouth twice daily with food (45 mg/m2/day) - continue
- Hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily - continue
- Folic acid 1 mg daily - continue
- Vitamin D3 2000 units daily - continue

Follow-up:
- Hematology/oncology clinic with repeat bone marrow in early 12/2025; ATRA consolidation to follow.
- Primary care within 2 weeks.
- Call for fever, bleeding, new headache or shortness of breath.

Looks well. Color improved. Petechiae resolved. No bruising. CV RRR. Lungs clear. Abd soft, no HSM.

A/P:

RTC after hem/onc visit or prn.

reports.text: Specimen: bone marrow aspirate and core biopsy, left posterior iliac crest. Clinical history: relapsed acute promyelocytic leukemia on tretinoin. Findings: normocellular marrow for age with trilineage hematopoiesis and orderly maturation; no increase in promyelocytes or blasts.

Hi Nilda - I read hematology's letter. Congratulations on finishing treatment and on the clean PCR!

documents.title: Emergency Department Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Arrival: 04/27/2026 14:25

CHIEF COMPLAINT: hearing voices, paranoid thoughts x 2 days.

HPI: 38 y/o F brought in by family. For the past two days she has been hearing voices that tell her someone is following her and that her relatives are in danger. She has paranoid beliefs to the same effect. No previous psychiatric history. Relevant history: systemic lupus erythematosus; rheumatology put her on high-dose prednisone about 11 days ago for a bad flare. She denies any recent stressors, denies illicit drug use and denies alcohol misuse.

PMH: systemic lupus erythematosus; relapsed acute promyelocytic leukemia, in second complete remission; hypergonadotropic hypogonadism.
PSH: none.
Home medications (per outside medication list):
- Hydroxychloroquine 200 mg PO daily
- Folic acid 1 mg PO daily
- Vitamin D3 2000 units PO daily
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother - rheumatoid arthritis; maternal aunt - SLE; father - hypertension.
SH: teacher. Never smoker. No alcohol misuse, no illicit drugs.

VITALS: BP 126/78, HR 94, RR 18, T 36.8 C, SpO2 99% RA - within normal limits.
EXAM: Restless and agitated. Appears to be responding to internal stimuli. Neuro: no focal neurologic deficits. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen benign.

LABS:
Na 140, K 4.1, Cl 102, HCO3 24, BUN 18, Cr 0.9, glucose 98, Ca 9.2.
CBC within normal limits (WBC 9.1).
Urine toxicology screen: negative.

MDM: acute onset of auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusions with no prior psychiatric history, beginning about 9 days into high-dose prednisone. Metabolic panel, CBC and toxicology unremarkable.
Impression: medication-induced (corticosteroid) psychosis.
- Psychiatry consulted in the ED - see separate note.
- Olanzapine 5 mg PO at bedtime started per psychiatry.
- Rheumatology on call reached by phone; agrees to begin tapering prednisone - their office will contact her with the schedule.
- Placed in ED observation overnight with family at bedside.

documents.title: Psychiatry consultation - ED
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
PSYCHIATRY CONSULTATION - EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Seen: 04/27/2026 18:30
Requested by: ED physician, for new-onset psychotic symptoms.

History: 38-year-old woman, no psychiatric history, two days of hearing voices warning that she is being followed and that harm will come to her family, with paranoid ideas in keeping with the voices. Began high-dose prednisone (60 mg daily) for a lupus flare on 04/16. Denies prior episodes of depression, mania or psychosis. Denies substance use; urine toxicology negative.

Mental status: restless, guarded but cooperative with family present. Speech normal in rate and volume. Affect tense. Thought process mostly linear. Thought content: persecutory delusions as above. Perception: auditory hallucinations, appears to be attending to them during interview. Denies suicidal or homicidal ideation. Insight partial, judgment fair.

Impression: medication-induced psychotic disorder, corticosteroid.

Recommendations:
1. Olanzapine 5 mg at bedtime.
2. Steroid taper as directed by rheumatology.
3. Overnight ED observation; reassess in the morning. If calmer and safe, may go home with family.
4. Outpatient follow-up with PCP within one week; return for worsening symptoms or any safety concern.

ED FOLLOW-UP

38F, SLE with severe flare (prednisone 60 mg started 4/16 by rheum), relapsed APL in second CR (ATRA finished 3/18), seen in ED 4/27-4/28 for corticosteroid-induced psychosis; started olanzapine 5 mg qhs.

Since discharge: voices and paranoid thoughts stopped around 4/30 and haven't returned. Sleeping well. Calm. She has good insight - describes the voices as "the steroid talking" and was frightened by how real they seemed. Joints much better and the facial rash has faded. Taking prednisone taper exactly as rheum wrote it; on schedule. No SI/HI.

Wrists and knees without swelling. No malar rash.

A/P:
1. Corticosteroid-induced psychosis - resolved symptomatically. Continue olanzapine 5 mg qhs for now; plan to stop in about 4 weeks if she stays well.
2. SLE flare - improving; continue prednisone taper per rheum and HCQ.
